answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens and form peer-auditing graphs. When identities wander across clusters, topological cut verifications detect sparse boundaries around fake nodes. Multi-agent committees audit suspicious interactions; any attempt to forge transactions triggers stake slashing. Because coordinated fraud requires cutting expansive graph neighborhoods, audit thresholds scale attacker cost superlinear to network size, rendering fake identities as futile as clearing a vast timber forest with a single blade.
